Fetch these three Amazon product pages and report exactly what each one is. Amazon often blocks automated fetches — if a page fails or returns a CAPTCHA/robot page, say so plainly for that URL rather than guessing.

URL 1: https://www.amazon.com/EC-Buying-TSL2591-Breakout-Development/dp/B0C1C55P57
URL 2: https://www.amazon.com/Teyleten-Robot-MLX90614-MLX90614ESF-Temperature/dp/B0CLDGFQYS
URL 3: https://www.amazon.com/Temperature-Barometric-Environmental-Compatible-Raspberry/dp/B0GRRDXGH8

For each URL that loads, report:
- The exact full product title
- The price
- The exact sensor chip part number stated anywhere on the page (title, bullets, or description)
- The operating voltage (3.3V, 5V, or both)
- The interface (I2C / SPI)

Then, specifically for each:

URL 1: Confirm whether the light sensor chip is a TSL2591 (not a TSL2561, TSL2550, BH1750, or other).

URL 2: Report the exact MLX90614 variant suffix if stated — e.g. MLX90614ESF-BAA, -BCI, -DCI, -DCC. Also report whether the board is described as GY-906, and whether it says GY-906-BAA or GY-906-DCI. Report the stated operating voltage.

URL 3: This is the critical one. Report whether the page says BME280 or BMP280, and quote the exact text where it names the chip. Crucially: report whether the listing claims to measure HUMIDITY, or only temperature and barometric pressure. A BME280 measures temperature + humidity + pressure; a BMP280 measures only temperature + pressure. Quote any sentence mentioning humidity. Also note if the title/bullets/description contradict each other about the chip, and whether this appears to be a sponsored listing.

Report findings only — do not add purchasing advice.
